newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo in talks with P&O despite protest.
newsitem.headline: Colombo in talks with P&O despite protest.

text.p: The Sri Lanka Ports Authority was continuing talks with Britain's Peninsula & Oriental Shipping Co for a deal to set up a container terminal at Colombo port despite protests by union workers, its chairman Sundra Jayawardena said on Thursday.

"We want to develop the southern part of the port to have at least another six deep-draft berths, for fifth and sixth generation ships, with a capacity of two million containers per year," he told Reuters.
The project is estimated to cost hundreds of millions of U.S. dollars and take ten years to build, he said.
The Colombo port's biggest labour union with 6,000 members staged a four-hour work stoppage to protest at the deal on Thursday, Jayawardena said.
Under the deal being negotiated, P&O and local partner John Keells Holdings will develop the Queen Elizabeth Quay, one of the port's two main quays, and the adjacent sea area.
The present capacity of the port, south Asia's trans-shipment hub, was 1.6 million containers, he said.
"We don't have the money to build," Jayawardena said. "If we don't build in time we'll lose to other ports which are not as well-placed geographically as Colombo."
"Now we use more than 85 percent of our capacity," Jayawardena said.
"According to international practice by the time a port gets up to 80 percent of capacity, any forward-looking port will plan out expansion," he added.
